messages:

Subject: Trace ID masking & request/response logging — post-call recap and next steps

Hi Linda / Tom,

Thanks again for your time today — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can line up the right folks on both sides.

Call recap (short):
- You run user-facing payments workflows; logs currently include request/response bodies and HTTP headers with X-Trace-Id values.
- Priority: avoid exposing PII in logs while preserving traceability for debugging and fraud investigations.
- Requirements flagged: 12+ months retention for transaction metadata, dual residency (US + EU) for EU user data, and the ability to produce redacted logs for audits.

Open questions we promised to confirm:
1) Which attributes are considered PII for FinPay in-scope (examples: card PAN, email, full name, masked PAN allowed?)
2) For trace IDs specifically — do you need the raw trace token preserved for correlation, or is a consistent pseudonymized ID acceptable?
3) Do you want redaction at ingest (redact before persisting) or post-processing (persist then redact on export)?

Attachments I shared during the call: audit-reqs-worksheet.xlsx (your copy), redaction-overview.pdf (our approach).

Proposed next steps:
- Technical deep-dive with your infra/security team and our runtime team to review sample logs and a proposed masking approach (we recommend a HMAC+pseudonymized-id flow, can support key rotation).
- Share a short logging schema sample from your side (anonymized) before the meeting.
- Prepare a draft of our proposed retention/residency controls to align on retention windows and exportability for audits.

Can you confirm availability for a 60-minute deep-dive on Tue 2026-07-21? If so, please share the names of your security and infra participants and any pre-read (sample log lines) you can provide.

Best,
Jonas

From: Linda Park <linda@finpay.co>

Date: 2026-07-18T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Trace ID masking & request/response logging — post-call recap and next steps

Thanks Jonas — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- PII in-scope: full card PAN (never in cleartext), full email address, customer full name, and internal customer_id. Masked PAN (last 4) is acceptable in logs.
- Trace IDs: we prefer pseudonymized trace IDs that remain consistent for a given request across services (so we can stitch flows) but must not be reversible to the original token.
- Redaction timing: preference is redaction-at-ingest for request/response bodies so we never persist raw PII.
- Retention: 13 months for transaction metadata; exceptions for fraud investigations are handled via an access request process.
- Residency: primary retention in US-EAST, EU user data must be retained in EU-WEST.

We can attend Tue 2026-07-21 10:00–11:00 PT for the deep-dive. I'll invite our security lead (sec@finpay.co) and Tom will bring a sample log extract (anonymized).

Also: could you send a short note on your masking approach (algorithm and key management) and whether Redwood supports redaction of specific headers (e.g., X-Trace-Id) versus pseudonymization?

Thanks,
Linda Park
Head of Platform Security, FinPay
linda@finpay.co

Marissa / Neha — forwarding FinPay's replies and details. Short ask: can you review and confirm our recommended approach below before the deep-dive?

Quoted: 
> From: Linda Park <linda@finpay.co>
> PII in-scope: full card PAN (never in cleartext), full email address, customer full name, and internal customer_id. Masked PAN (last 4) is acceptable in logs.
> Trace IDs: preference for consistent, pseudonymized trace IDs (non-reversible).
> Redaction timing: preference is redaction-at-ingest.
> Retention: 13 months for transaction metadata; EU user data stored in EU-WEST.

Our proposed technical pattern (high level):
- Ingest-level transform: run a small transform layer in front of the request/response logging pipeline that:
  - Uses field-based rules to remove/replace PII (e.g., full PAN => remove, email => hash(email) with salt).
  - For trace IDs, we can either redact header values or replace with a stable pseudonym generated via HMAC-SHA256(trace_id, tenant_key) truncated to 32 chars. This preserves consistent correlation across services but is non-reversible without the tenant_key.
  - Store original raw logs only in a single encrypted hotbox with extremely restricted access for fraud investigations (audit trail + Just-In-Time access).

Notes for security: key rotation support, KMS/HSM integration for tenant_key, audit logging for access requests.

Action items before Tue:
- Marissa: confirm this pattern meets our security posture and whether we should recommend additional measures (e.g., differential privacy on certain fields, tokenization service).
- Neha: prepare a brief sample config we can show FinPay that demonstrates ingest transform rules and a sample of before/after log lines. I attached an internal draft: MVP-mask-approach.docx.

I'll set the deep-dive invite for Tue 2026-07-21 10:00 PT and include your teams + FinPay.

Thanks,
Jonas

Linda / Tom — great, thanks for confirming. Calendar invite sent for Tue 2026-07-21 10:00–11:00 PT. Zoom link: https://zoom.us/j/9876543210?pwd=example (also in shared Drive).

A few pre-reads and commitments from our side before the deep-dive:
- We will provide a short sample of the ingest transform showing: original log line -> redacted log line -> pseudonymized-trace-id example.
- Our recommended approach for trace IDs: HMAC-SHA256(trace_id, tenant_kms_key) truncated to 32 chars. Key stored in your preferred KMS; Redwood supports integrations with AWS KMS and customer HSMs. This yields consistent pseudonyms and is non-reversible without the key.
- Redaction timing: we support redaction-at-ingest out-of-the-box via our logging transform. For customers who require raw retention for forensic work, we can stage raw records to an encrypted, access-controlled store (requires approval and audit-trailed access requests).

Next steps for FinPay: please upload an anonymized sample log extract to the Drive folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cExample) and confirm the names of the security/infrastructure folks joining. Our deep-dive agenda will be:
1) Review sample lines and walk through before/after transform.
2) Discuss residency and retention enforcement (how to split US vs EU retention).
3) Cover access controls and audit process for raw logs.

If you have any concerns about the HMAC approach or need a different pattern (e.g., reversible tokenization with KMS-wrapped tokens), flag them in reply and we'll add to the agenda.

Thanks — looking forward to Tuesday.

Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
